_source: Our own table: the designed cores of IV's fission reactor (docs/eras/iv.md, 'Designed-core reactor' and 'Decisions taken with the raise', decision 3). Real physics: light-water PWR cores, CANDU-style heavy-water moderators that pick up tritium, MOX fuel and fast breeders with a U-238 blanket.
_how_it_is_used: Read by startup_scripts/grindless/iv/fission_reactor.js (published as global.grindless.fissionReactor.cores) and turned into one gtceu:fission_core recipe per core by server_scripts/grindless/iv/fission_reactor.js, id grindless:fission_core/<name>. The smoke test gg_test_fission_reactor.js checks the live recipes against this table.

A recipe is one channel-cycle of one core: cycleTicks long, the programmed circuit picks the core (GTM's recipe lookup would hide a light-water recipe that is a prefix of the heavy-water one), the fuel assembly is a chanced input (wearChance of 10000: an assembly lasts 10000 / wearChance channel-cycles) and the spent assembly a chanced output (spentChance of 10000). GTM 7.5.3's OR chance logic keeps a remainder per machine, so in practice exactly one assembly is used up, and one spent assembly comes out, every 200 channel-cycles.

Every channel takes the coolant (it is lost through the vents) and, for a core with a moderator, moderator.amount mB of moderator.fluid, which comes out as the same amount of moderator.becomes (the moderator is activated: heavy water picks up tritium, decision 3).

The reactor runs up to `channels` copies of a recipe at once (lib/generators.js): one per assembly in its input buses, as far as the coolant, the moderator, the room for the outputs and the dynamo hatches allow. euPerChannel is the EU/t of one channel. These recipes are NOT doubled by power/generators.js: the numbers here are final.
